summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, and anoxic brain injury was admitted for evaluation of chest pain that occurred after coughing during a dialysis session. The pain was sharp, midline, and resolved spontaneously, differing from his prior cardiac pain. Workup showed no EKG changes, troponin levels were within his baseline, and imaging revealed no pulmonary edema or acute cardiac issues. The pain was determined to be musculoskeletal in origin, likely due to coughing from a viral illness. Hyperkalemia was noted but managed with dialysis. He remained hemodynamically stable, completed a dialysis session, and was discharged home with aspirin restarted and instructions to follow up with his specialists.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
